questions.text: Tell me about a hiring process you built or fixed. What was broken and what did you change?
questions.rationale: Process-building stories separate operators from administrators.

questions.text: Describe a time you coached a manager through their first underperformance conversation. What did you tell them?
questions.rationale: Manager enablement is the highest-leverage people ops skill.

questions.text: Walk me through an investigation you handled. How did you protect fairness for everyone involved?
questions.rationale: Investigation discipline under confidentiality constraints is a defining senior skill.

questions.text: How do you keep compliance work from making the company feel bureaucratic? Give an example.
questions.rationale: Tests whether the candidate can deliver protection without friction theater.

questions.text: Tell me about a policy you wrote that people actually followed. Why did it stick?
questions.rationale: Policy adoption is a design problem; sticky policies evidence user-centered thinking.

questions.text: Describe a layoff or restructure you supported. What did you fight for in how it was done?
questions.rationale: Conduct during the hardest people moments reveals values under pressure.

questions.text: What drew you to people operations? What do you actually love about the work?
questions.rationale: Separates genuine people-systems interest from default HR career drift.

questions.text: How do you run compensation review cycles fairly when budgets are tight? Walk me through your last one.
questions.rationale: Comp fairness under constraint is where people ops credibility is won or lost.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a leader whose decision would hurt the team. What happened?
questions.rationale: Spine with power is non-negotiable in this role; needs a real story.

questions.text: Describe your onboarding program. What does a new hire's first week actually look like?
questions.rationale: Concrete first-week detail exposes whether onboarding is designed or improvised.

questions.text: How do you measure whether your people programs work? Give an example of one you sunset for not working.
questions.rationale: Program-killing discipline separates evidence-driven people ops from initiative accumulation.

questions.text: Tell me about mediating a conflict between two employees. What was your approach and outcome?
questions.rationale: Mediation method reveals neutrality, structure, and follow-through.

questions.text: What does a genuinely useful performance review process look like to you? How close have you gotten to building one?
questions.rationale: Everyone hates reviews; tests whether the candidate has moved past complaint to design.

questions.text: Describe the trickiest confidentiality situation you have navigated. How did you decide what to share?
questions.rationale: Confidentiality judgment is daily people ops terrain and hard to fake.

questions.text: How do you support managers hiring for roles you do not understand technically?
questions.rationale: Tests structured-interview instincts: process expertise complementing domain expertise.

questions.text: Tell me about a benefits or perks decision you influenced. How did you weigh cost against impact?
questions.rationale: Commercial thinking applied to people programs; screens for tradeoff literacy.

questions.text: What would employees at your last company say about the HR team? What would you say they got wrong about you?
questions.rationale: Perception awareness plus a chance to show non-defensive reflection.

questions.text: Describe building or updating an employee handbook. What did you cut?
questions.rationale: The cutting question screens for judgment over accumulation.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to apply a policy to a leader who thought it did not apply to them.
questions.rationale: Consistency under status pressure is the integrity test of the function.

questions.text: How do you stay current on employment law without becoming the department of no?
questions.rationale: Tests learning habit plus the enabling-versus-blocking framing choice.

questions.text: Walk me through an engagement survey cycle you ran. What did you do with the worst result?
questions.rationale: Survey follow-through is where most programs die; the worst-result answer is the signal.

questions.text: Describe your experience with HRIS or people systems. Tell me about a migration or implementation you survived.
questions.rationale: Systems implementation experience is checkable and predicts operational capability.

questions.text: What is your philosophy on structured versus unstructured interviews? What does the evidence say, and what do you do in practice?
questions.rationale: Tests evidence literacy on the exact problem this product exists to solve.

questions.text: Tell me about the first sixty days in a company where you were the first people hire. What did you triage?
questions.rationale: Sequencing instinct in a department-of-one context, common in startup people ops.

questions.text: How have you handled a manager who consistently produces attrition on their team?
questions.rationale: Pattern accountability for managers is a senior move requiring courage and data.

questions.text: What people ops trend do you think is overhyped right now, and what deserves more attention?
questions.rationale: Independent thinking about the field beats recitation of its orthodoxy.

questions.text: Describe a time you improved diversity of a hiring pipeline through process changes rather than targets.
questions.rationale: Process-based inclusion work is checkable and legally sound; tests practical fluency.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were the only person in the room advocating for an employee's side.
questions.rationale: The advocacy instinct under social pressure, evidenced concretely.

questions.text: What kind of company culture brings out your best work, and where have you struggled?
questions.rationale: Honest fit assessment; the struggle half is the informative half.

questions.text: How do you keep your own judgment fair when you personally dislike someone involved in a case?
questions.rationale: Bias management in the person who manages bias processes; meta but essential.
